summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of orthotopic liver transplant, alcoholic cirrhosis, cervical spine hardware erosion into the esophagus, and chronic immunosuppression, was admitted for a painful rash on the left chest and back. He was diagnosed with non-disseminated herpes zoster in the T6 dermatome. Treatment included intravenous acyclovir initially, transitioned to oral valacyclovir, with improved pain control using gabapentin, increased oxycodone, and hydromorphone. His immunosuppressive regimen of mycophenolate and prednisone was continued, and fludrocortisone was reinstated after being omitted from the hospital medication list. Chronic issues including malnutrition, cervical hardware erosion, diarrhea, and chronic pain were stable and managed conservatively. He was discharged home on a walker with follow-up planned with transplant infectious disease, hepatology, and primary care, continuing antiviral suppression and all baseline medications.
